Retain-value (inScope:true + optional on whenFalse) is animals' one exception (regionOfOriginCode) and is not proposed anywhere in plants. Source: skeleton docs/scope-and-wipe.md, model/obligations/evaluator.js, bridge/purge.js; live-animals scope-and-wipe. Source: live-animals opening-run (flow/run.js); skeleton opening-run (run-state.js, kit.js:110-120). kit.errorSummary builds one govukErrorSummary titled There is a problem with one entry per field error linking to #fieldName (custom href builder when the fix lives on another page, e.g. CYA party errors); the page title is prefixed Error: when a summary is present; field errors render inline via errorMessage; input name, id and error-map key stay identical so the summary link moves focus to the control. Plants answers EVERY validation failure with HTTP 400 — animals is inconsistent (seven pages return 200 with the error page; live-animals note) and that inconsistency is not copied. Source: live-animals error-summary-conventions; skeleton gds-error-wiring.

Every persistence write is wrapped in kit.recoverableSave(): a backend failure classed recoverable re-renders the page with a govukNotificationBanner role=alert (There is a problem: Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.) and HTTP 500, keeping the submitted values; a STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN error redirects to the same URL with ?staleAction=1, which shows The notification has been updated banner. Every form posts a hidden crumb (CSRF) and a hidden concurrencyToken from the loaded journey; the backend mints a new token on each save and rejects a stale one. Source: live-animals recoverable-save, concurrency-and-csrf; skeleton controller-contract, persistence-and-mapper. Serves NNS-UN-009 (complete dependably).

Three journey-scoped cookies, base64json, httpOnly, SameSite Lax, no ttl, named in journeys/linear/config.js and never shared with animals: highRiskPlantsKnownJourneys (ids this session may list/act on), highRiskPlantsOpeningRun (RUN_ACTIVE/RUN_COMPLETE per journey), highRiskPlantsFlowOnlyAnswers (declaration per journey). Radio and select pages validate with oneOf (reject only values outside the offered list) and let a blank answer through so a trader can Save and return with the row still In progress; text inputs validate max length and pattern only. Pages that DO require at page level, copied from animals' split: country of origin (requiredOneOf), the declaration, and collection entry fields at add time (category, and the fields it reveals — mirroring animals' document add fields). Plants additionally requires at page level: commodityType (the entry gate; nothing downstream makes sense without it), arrivalStatus and arrivalDate (the timing rules hang on them). The obligation status, not the page, holds the hub row and the submit gate. Source: live-animals lenient-page-validation (import-reason/controller.js:25); skeleton validation-library.

Two obligations are strictly-earlier prerequisites enforced when the user continues: commodityType and countryOfOrigin (ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE in bridge/obligation-source.js, empty today). Derived page gates hold every later page and section until they are answered and the hub shows Cannot start yet on blocked rows. Mirrors animals' countryOfOrigin + commoditySelection pair. Source: skeleton system-populated-and-enforced-at-continue (obligation-source.js:29-35, prerequisites.js:13-32); live-animals enforced-at-continue.

One org-scoped, typeless address book serves every role (INS-owned, read-only here; writes belong to the INS frontend). Organisation id comes only from the verified session, never the payload. Source: live-animals address-book-picker, addresses-hub-page; skeleton addressBook service (address-book/index.js:94-132), answers-read-sanitiser-unwired. Under c-026 and NNS-UN-034 (accurate, structured location).

Left column: Filter notifications (Keyword or reference input, Search). Right column: results label (No Results / Showing 1 Result / Showing {a} to {b} of {n} Results), Sort by (Arrival newest/oldest, Date created newest/oldest; default arrivalDate desc) with Update sort, one govuk-summary-card per notification (title = reference; rows Commodity | Origin | Arrival, Consignor | Status tag (+ Late tag); Date created | Date submitted), per-status actions, pagination, empty text 'You have not started any notifications in this session.', success banners after ?deleted=1 / ?copied=1. Plants swaps the animal-specific cells (Commodity = commodityType + first line category/genus; Arrival = arrivalDate). Source: live-animals dashboard-listing (features/dashboard/controller.js); skeleton dashboardReserved. Provisional pick under c-033. | Ruled at D4-parties-and-contact (d-014, c-026): The Consignor cell shows nothing for potato notifications (consignor out of scope — c-026). | Ruled at D6-chrome-and-journey-shape (d-068, c-033), superseding 'Provisional pick under c-033.': Ruled under c-033: per-set plants list, same-as-animals structure, no type filter, no journey-type label.

Dates use the MoJ date picker through kit.dateField: one text box, format d/m/yyyy, width-10, optional min/max as d/m/yyyy text attributes; kit.readDate parses to { day, month, year } (or passes the raw string through so dateText can reject it); stored as the parts object; validated with dateText, or dateTextInRange once a window is ruled (c-029). Source: live-animals date-entry (shared/kit.js:199); skeleton date-fields, validation-library.

Long lists that need type-ahead (countryOfOrigin, genus, proposedPlaceOfLanding) use appAccessibleAutocomplete over a select with showAllValues and a noResults message, listing only a placeholder plus the real options; short fixed lists (commodityType, category, arrivalStatus) are govukRadios with per-option hints. The accessible-autocomplete component already ships under common/components in the plants engine. Source: live-animals select-and-autocomplete-widgets (origin/template.njk:18); skeleton templates-and-nunjucks-roots.

Every templated feature owns copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and copy/copy.test.js; controllers call copyFor({ en, cy }) which today always resolves en (no locale toggle, cookie or lang attribute exists in animals or the plants engine); copy-parity.test.js enforces that cy mirrors en path-for-path, kind-for-kind and arity-for-arity and that every string leaf differs from English unless registered in IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST under '<module>:<leafPath>' with a justification (codes, proper nouns, 'GB', reference formats). Every cy file is headed MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator; the spec copies animals' Welsh only where the English is verbatim animals and invents none. Source: live-animals welsh-copy-seam; skeleton copy-convention, copy-parity, copy-parity-allowlist-key. The Annex 6 requirement for a live Welsh service (annex:6/non-functional/item:7) is the separate open question nfr-english-and-welsh.

Three guards run in routes.js before routes are added, so a partial increment fails the server start, not a test: (1) buildDispatch -> assertFullCoverage throws 'Obligations collected by no page' for any obligation at any depth no page names in collects (via nearest-ancestor ownership) that is not in SYSTEM_POPULATED — the four system obligations (referenceNumber, dateOfNotification, notificationStatus, lateNotificationIndicator) must be listed there or live on the record envelope; (2) createFulfilmentRegistry throws 'obligations owned by no feature' for any unbound leaf and 'must import its obligation object from the manifest' on identity mismatch; (3) assertObligationPurity throws on any label/title/titleKey/hint/legend/widget key in the obligation graph. spec-lint.sh pre-flights guard 1. Every plants obligation therefore lands with its page, its scalar()/grouped() binding and its copy in one increment. Source: skeleton boot-guard-dispatch-coverage, boot-guard-binding-coverage, boot-guard-manifest-identity (dispatch.js:71-90, fulfilment-registry.js:156-163, no-display-keys.js:24-31).

Obligations carry identity, scope, mandate and invariants only — every label, hint, option text and error message in this spec lives in the owning feature's copy pair (the spec's label/hint/errorCopy fields are for the copy pass, never the manifest). applyTo rules are built only from the helper library: equalsGate/includesGate for the notification-level commodityType gates; allowListed(category, <list>, null projection) for the same-frame per-line gates on category; anyAllowListed(category, potatoCategories) if a notification-level rule ever needs to read the lines (the origin narrowing is validation, not applyTo); branchedGate with predicateMeta as the escape hatch. Each allow-list comes from the set-owned commodities service and is pinned by obligations/whitelists.test.js. Source: skeleton model-purity, applyto-helper-vocabulary, helper-selection-rule, obligation-shape (helpers/index.js:32-87, no-display-keys.js:24-31).

copy-convention.test.js and copy-parity.test.js are ARMED against the empty features folder: each asserts readdirSync(features) is [] and fails with a message telling the author to restore the per-feature checks. The first feature increment (dashboard) must, in the same commit, rewrite copy-convention's per-feature half (walk every feature dir, require the copy triple, forbid root-level copy files, check every leaf with isCopyLeaf) and extend copy-parity's modulePairs to every feature's copy/ pair (later plus the flow/section-captions pair), keeping IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST justified. Declared as two restore extras anchored after the dashboard page. Source: skeleton tripwire-copy-convention, tripwire-copy-parity (copy-convention.test.js:8-27, copy-parity.test.js:16-51). | Ruling: The dashboard increment rewrites copy-convention.test.js and copy-parity.test.js in the same commit as the first feature folder; the two restore extras (restore-copy-convention-tripwire, restore-copy-parity-tripwire) are withdrawn and their detail folds into the dashboard increment's plan. The flow/section-captions pair still joins copy-parity with wire-section-captions.

A collecting controller: one render() helper for GET and POST errors built on kit.base(title, {backLink, journey, page}); GET calls state.get() once and prefills from answers; POST reads raw payload values, validates with lib/validate (service-backed membership rules built INSIDE POST so they see data primed at boot — the category-by-commodityType and origin-by-category narrowings are exactly this), re-renders raw values with status 400 on error, commits cleaned values with state.commit() (never the raw payload), redirects through await kit.nextTarget(request, page, committed.scope); routes = kit.pageRoutes(page, { get, post }). Only obligation names and declared flow-only keys may be committed — helper form fields (index, action, search) are stripped first or assertRecognisedAnswerKeys throws. Every page routes through kit.base so captions and hubHref arrive uniformly (animals' hub/dashboard/CYA controllers that hand-build view models are not copied). Source: skeleton controller-contract, answer-key-recognition, validation-library; live-animals INCONSISTENT chrome assembly note.

commodityLines is the recipe's two-page batch shape: the commodities list page owns the group (collects names only the root), the commodity-details entry sub-page adds one line (appendEntryAt) or edits one by ?index (updateEntryAt after looking the instance up and refusing an index the collection has no entry for), Remove on the list posts remove:<index> (removeEntryAt; Number.isInteger guard), and a leaf-less entry is never persisted. Positions are snapshot-local, never ids. requires.minEntries 1 with errorCode obligation.commodityLines.atLeastOne is the floor; there is no sibling-count cap (MAX_ENTRIES_FROM stays empty) and no nested collection. The change context threads through the loop (only the exiting Continue repoints to CYA). Source: skeleton collections-engine-api, cardinality-requires, cardinality-cap, fulfilment-index-tokens; live-animals commodity-batch-search, per-line-cards-and-caps (the search-then-tick and cap machinery are not needed).

Reference data that only makes sense for plants — the three commodityType values, the nine category values and their grouping by type, the fifteen genus entries and the hardwood narrowing, the per-category allow-lists every per-line gate reads, the origin-country narrowing per category — belongs under sets/high-risk-plants/services/commodities as a set-owned service wired through a configure* seam in routes.js, with a stub and (later) a real client, and obligations/whitelists.test.js checking each allow-list against it so a hand-typed list cannot drift. Created by the commodities increment. Policy requires the list to be amendable without a code release (commodity-list-dynamic-and-maintainable) — the service boundary is where that lands. Source: skeleton set-owned-services-seam (docs/services.md); phnns-policy annex:1/closing-para, annex:6/functional/item:4; live-animals STUB-ONLY reference data note (do not copy the name-keyed allow-list vocabulary).

src/server/app/contract.test.js is a manual L1 table pinning that each collecting controller's valid POST commits exactly the committable names in its meta.collects (with any scope seed that brings conditional obligations into scope — e.g. commodityType=potatoes for arrivalTime). The file does not exist; the first plants collecting controller (commodity-type) recreates it and every later collecting page adds a case; only npm test runs it. Declared as a restore extra anchored after commodity-type. Source: skeleton contract-test-table, missing-tests-and-fixtures.

Per feature: controller.test.js (Vitest through the engine with stub services), copy/copy.test.js and a co-located *.fit.spec.js (fit/<page>.fit.spec.js for multi-page groups) that starts its own notification, uses role/label/visible-copy locators imported from copy.en.js, never sleeps, has no page-object layer, and covers initial render, happy-path save and redirect, reload persistence, each validation rule, value preservation on error, every error-summary link moving focus, Back / Save and return / Cancel / Change navigation, conditional scope-skip-purge, CYA rows and Change links, and the hub row states. Accessibility: AxeBuilder withTags wcag2a + wcag2aa on the initial render AND the validation-error state, failing on serious or critical. Set tests: obligations/coverage.test.js (first obligation), whitelists.test.js (first allow-list), flow/task-rows.test.js (first task row). Serves annex:6/non-functional/item:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA) at the page level. Source: skeleton fit-spec-conventions, missing-tests-and-fixtures; live-animals feature-test-conventions. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-074, nfr-accessible-wcag-2-2-aa), superseding 'AxeBuilder withTags wcag2a + wcag2aa on the initial render AND the validation-error state, failing on serious or critical.': AxeBuilder withTags [wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa] on the initial render AND the validation-error state, failing on serious or critical (axe-core 4.12.1 tags rules by WCAG version; the two 2.0 tags alone skip every 2.1 and 2.2 rule — diverges from animals' two-tag list on the strength of annex:6/non-functional/item:1, WCAG 2.2 AA). The first page increment writes the same list into sets/high-risk-plants/docs/add-a-page.md (Accessibility test); any violation the wider list surfaces is a finding to fix, never a reason to narrow the list.

Every plants increment ends green on, from the repo root: npm run test:high-risk-plants; npm test (pretest builds the frontend; runs the L1 tripwires and the contract table — the only command that does); npm run format:check; npm run lint (eslint neostandard + sonarjs, stylelint gds, depcruise); PORT=3053 npm run test:fit:features; npm run test:fit:journeys when the whole journey or shared FIT helpers change. Green means every command exits 0 with no failed tests and no lint errors; while a suite matches no files, say so rather than reporting coverage. The husky pre-commit hook runs format:check, lint and test. Source: skeleton verification-ladder (package.json:13-50, .husky/pre-commit).

playwright.config.js defines two fit projects against a self-started STUB_MODE server (default port 3003; PORT=3053 when the workspace stack is up): features (every **/*.fit.spec.js under the set) and journeys (fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js driven by flow/fixtures/happy-path.json — neither exists). Both pass vacuously today (--pass-with-no-tests). The journeys project stays empty until the journey is walkable end to end, when the smoke spec and the happy-path fixture land together (a restore extra at the end of the backlog); the five mural use cases seed that fixture (use-cases-as-test-fixtures). Deployed multi-service E2E lives in the tests repo as a fourth Playwright project (declared e2e extras). Source: skeleton playwright-projects, tests-repo-plants-project-absent; live-animals feature-test-conventions (fit journeys project).

npm run lint:arch enforces the four layers: only routes.js imports sets/**; L2 (engine/model/bridge/flow/services/lib/shared/analysis) never imports sets; obligations never import journeys; one journey never imports a sibling; sets never import L1; the engine never imports services; the bridge never imports engine/flow/analysis/kit (three bridge->flow violations are baselined in .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json — a declared chore); no circular imports. Plants set code may import L2 APIs and its own set only; a feature that needs the evaluator goes through the engine/bridge. Source: skeleton layer-rules-depcruise (.dependency-cruiser.cjs:13-175), depcruise-known-violations-baselined.

Canonical UUID-keyed fulfilment is the durable answer source: every write replaces a whole evaluated-and-purged snapshot through the records port (create, load, list, has, replaceFulfilment, finalise, amend, cancelAmend, copy, softDelete, clear); reads rebuild projected answers, scope and status so derived state is never stored; one journey load per request. The real adapter derives the backend NotificationDto through notification-mapper/index.js, which today projects referenceNumber and nothing else — the plants backend has no typed content fields, so every plants obligation round-trips through the opaque fulfilments payload. Mapper A only: no Mapper B, no outbox, no event publishing, no PIMS routing, no document upload (epic EUDPA-407). A typed backend field for any plants obligation is a backend-schema decision recorded as an open question, with an explicit omission assertion until then. Source: skeleton persistence-and-mapper (docs/persistence.md, notification-mapper/index.js:1-12).

STUB_MODE is one service-wide switch (refused in production): a stub run serves stub reference data, the stub records/session adapters, and signs its own session via /auth/stub-sign-in?organisationId=<org> (default stub-org-1, user STUB0001/2100010101) — auth is still enforced. Real mode uses Defra ID OIDC (/auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-in-oidc, /auth/organisation) and primes countries and ports at boot; /auth/sign-out and the layout's Log out link end the session; auth/unauthorised.njk is the failure view (hardcoded English — a chore). Sign-in is the only precondition to notifying built in this run (c-039). vitest and playwright both set STUB_MODE=true. Source: skeleton session-cookies-and-stub-mode, authSignIn, authSignOut, unauthorised pages.

Prefer server-rendered controls. When a page genuinely needs a client bundle (the accessible-autocomplete on origin, arrival-details and commodity-details already ships as a common component; any add-another or conditional-reveal enhancement beyond govuk radios), put its entry under journeys/linear/features/<name>/client/index.js, add a NAMED entry to the repo-root webpack.config.js, and load it from the template with getAssetPath('<entry>.js'). A missing webpack entry is silent: the page renders, the bundle URL 404s, nothing is logged — build config is load-bearing and the fit spec proves the behaviour. Source: skeleton client-js-webpack (webpack.config.js:22-24, docs/features.md).

Lighthouse CI audits URLs read from .lighthouse/targets.json (npm run lighthouse:targets), desktop preset, signing in first through the Defra ID stub, score floors performance 0.60 / accessibility 0.70 / best-practices 0.70 and NO SEO assertion (none should be added). The URL list is derived from registered routes, so every plants page joins the audit by being reachable after seeding: each needs a stable report name in scripts/lighthouse/audit-targets.js and a seed shape in seed-notification.js that satisfies its prerequisites (a page whose prerequisites are unmet redirects to the hub and silently audits the hub). Both scripts are missing — a fix extra at the start of the backlog — and each page increment adds its seed shape and report name. Source: skeleton lighthouse-expectations, lighthouse-scripts-missing (lighthouserc.cjs:1-54, scripts/lighthouse/).

'Ability to amend the notification before submitting' (annex:6/functional/item:12) and NNS-UN-007 ('confidence that the information I provide is complete and correct ... avoid errors') are met by save-and-return, the hub statuses, inline validation and the Check your answers page with a Change link on every row (cya-change-round-trip). The paper says nothing about amendment after submission — that is notification-actions-after-submission (open question, c-030).

'A decision was made at FTA-TCA group in February 2026 not to charge for these activities as they will be a public good. However, this position will be reviewed once cost data is available (i.e. 2028).' (section:fees-and-charges/para:1). There is no payment step, fee display or invoice reference anywhere in the journey.

The blueprint's Export certification stage reads 'No export cert required' with no actor node (file:blueprint/region:Export certification); the SI matters name no document; epic EUDPA-407 puts document uploads out of this run. The journey must not ask for, require or upload an export certificate, phytosanitary certificate or any other document — no documents collection, no upload page, no document references. Animals' documents feature (0..10 uploads with virus scanning) is not copied. Any later document requirement is document-uploads-out-of-scope (open question).

'Customs dec raised, but no SPS customs hold or matching required' (file:blueprint/region:Customs matching, no actor node). The notification is not matched to a customs declaration and does not hold goods, so the journey collects no customs reference (MRN, entry number) and no transport or port-of-exit details — none of animals' transport section is copied. Failure to notify is detected outside the service by cross-referencing customs and passport data (section:non-compliance/para:1), which is why the supplier, producer and crop identifiers must be matchable values.

'There will instead be a requirement to use EU plant passports, for higher risk material only (mainly plants for planting)' (section:policy/para:1-2). Plant passports are a separate regime: the notification does not ask for, upload or replace passport data. The supplier identification number and EPPO code are the only passport-adjacent values and are typed in, not extracted (import-from-existing-documents is parked).

'Receive information on WHAT is arriving WHEN and WHERE (the notification)' (annex:6/functional/item:1) and NNS-UN-021 (regulator: 'what is arriving, when, and where') are the spine of the journey and the section order: commodity (what) -> origin (where from) -> arrival (when) -> destination (where to) -> parties -> contact -> review. 'Ensure sufficient detail is captured to allow plant health inspectors to identify when spot checks are required' (annex:6/functional/item:3) is why category, genus, origin, destination and date are coded or structured, not free text.

The potato duty (annex:5/reg:24A) and the plants/wood duty (reg 26) are separate regulations with different matters and timing windows, and the mural splits data capture into 'Potatoes (ware and seed)' and 'Other goods' (data-fields-split-by-goods-type). A notification therefore carries exactly one commodityType chosen first; a mixed consignment is two notifications. The commodity-type hint says so. Mirrors animals' inset 'A separate notification is required for each health certificate' in role, not wording.

NNS-UN-010 ('proportionate and relevant so that I only provide information that is necessary for my consignment'), NNS-UN-004 ('simple ... minimal effort' — both bold on the page), NNS-UN-036 (questions depend on consignment status) and NNS-UN-011/013 (potato- and wood-specific sets) are met by scope: every conditional obligation is applyTo on commodityType or category, out-of-scope fields are neither rendered nor validated nor committed, arrival-status is skipped for potatoes, and the derived gates hide a page whose every obligation is out of scope. Article 9(7) OCR caps the data at what is strictly necessary (section:legal-basis/para:1) — no question outside the statutory matters and Common Data is asked. Source: skeleton derived-gates, scope-and-wipe.

'provide written notification to the competent authority of the matters referred to in paragraph (2)' (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)): the digital submission is the written notification, attributable to the signed-in Defra ID organisation and user, persisted as a SUBMITTED record with a unique reference, the date of notification and the declaration, and retrievable by the authority (NNS-UN-032 traceability). The signed-in organisation is the professional operator; no separate notifier identity is typed (c-038).

The entry page (commodity-type) is the one page whose back link depends on state: hub when the notification already has committed answers, dashboard otherwise. Every other page links back to the hub, except child pages (commodity-details -> commodities; contact-details -> consignment-contact-select) which link to their parent, pages reached with ?change=1 (-> check your answers), the declaration (-> notification-view) and the confirmation (no back link). Source: live-animals origin-back-link, confirmation-page. | Ruled at D4-parties-and-contact (d-013, c-025), superseding 'except child pages (commodity-details -> commodities; contact-details -> consignment-contact-select) which link to their parent': except child pages (commodity-details -> commodities) which link to their parent.

'Provide sufficient information for track and trace in the event of an outbreak detection' (annex:6/functional/item:5; section:justification/para:3 traceback/forward). The consignor, supplier identification number, producer and crop identification numbers, country of origin and place of destination / current location are the trace chain and are all captured as required matters; nothing extra is asked. Non-compliance detection cross-references customs, plant-passport and Seed Potato Classification Scheme data (section:non-compliance/para:1), so those identifiers are stored verbatim as entered.

'Examples of potential non-compliances include: Failure to making a notification; Incorrect notification details; Late notification' (section:non-compliance/para:2) with sanctions administered outside the service (section:non-compliance/para:3). A late or post-arrival notification is therefore ACCEPTED and recorded, never blocked: arrivalDate has no future-only rule, the declaration submits regardless of timing, and lateness is a flag (lateNotificationIndicator) shown to the notifier and the authority. The mural use case 'Ware potatoes from Spain/Portugal with a late notification' (file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:2) is a happy-path fixture, not an error case.

The five blueprint use cases (file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:1-5) — Ware potatoes from Spain/Poland; Ware potatoes from Spain/Portugal with a late notification; Seed potatoes from any EU country; Spruce (Picea) from any EU country; Conifer wood from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain — are the seed shapes for flow/fixtures/happy-path.json, the Lighthouse seed-notification.js SEED_SHAPES and the tests-repo journey specs: one potato pre-arrival, one potato late, one seed potato (origin outside the four ware countries), one plants-for-planting with genus/species/EPPO code, one wood with phytosanitary treatments and the four-country origin narrowing.

Animals is inconsistent: the contact page makes the fieldset legend the page heading (isPageHeading: true) and renders no caption, while every other single-question page renders an h1 plus a legend or label (live-animals note on contact/template.njk:12). Plants picks one convention: a single-question radios page (commodity-type, arrival-status) uses the legend as the page heading with the section caption above it; a single-input page uses an h1 with the label as the heading; the address pickers keep animals' h1 + description. consignment-contact-select stays exactly as animals (same-as-animals) — its bare, legend-as-heading shape is the source of the plants convention.

Stay in the govuk-frontend toolbox: Nunjucks macros from govuk-frontend 6.x and @ministryofjustice/frontend 10.x, govuk-* utility classes, the shipped accessible-autocomplete component; no hand-rolled components or custom CSS. Animals' bespoke classes (app-commodity-total*, notification-list__*, app-link-button, app-form-inline) and its custom hub totals panel are debt and are not copied; the plants dashboard cards and hub use govukSummaryCard and govukTaskList as-is. Source: live-animals OUTSIDE THE GOVUK TOOLBOX note; skeleton templates-and-nunjucks-roots; annex:6/non-functional/item:2 'Meets GDS standards'.

services/import-reason-purpose serves nothing (both label maps are {} — 'Deliberately empty. The journey's import reasons and purposes are not yet agreed') and has no real client. No plants source asks a reason-for-import or purpose question — the potato 'intended use' and the optional 'use' are free-text per-line matters — so the plants journey does not use this service and the platform's transport-reference and commercial-transporters services are likewise unused. Whether to delete or keep them is a declared chore at the start of the backlog. Source: skeleton import-reason-purpose-empty, importReasonPurpose/transportReference/commercialTransporters serviceOnly fields.

'New SPS rules on GOV.UK and Europa.EU' is the Guidance & comms stage (file:blueprint/region:Guidance & comms, actor Importer, agent) — guidance is published outside the service. NNS-UN-001 (understand whether my goods are high-risk and pre/post), NNS-UN-002 and NNS-UN-008 (understand what information is required, first time right) are met inside the journey by the dashboard intro copy, a GOV.UK guidance link, the commodity-type option hints (timing windows) and per-field hint text, not by separate guidance or before-you-start pages. A dedicated eligibility checker ('are my goods high-risk?') is the open question guidance-before-you-start.

Potatoes: 'at least two days before the expected date of their arrival' (section:policy/para:6/item:1; annex:5/reg:24A(1)); plants and wood: 'before or no later than four days after the date of their arrival' (section:policy/para:6/item:2; reg 26(1)); 'Highlight to the user (internal and external) when a notification was made outside of required timings' (annex:6/functional/item:2); NNS-UN-012 (importer told when late and what rule) and NNS-UN-014 (regulator sees late ones). Actor: importer and regulator. Proposed: submitJourney computes lateNotificationIndicator from arrivalDate, commodityType and dateOfNotification in Europe/London (potatoes: late if submitted after arrivalDate minus 2 days; plants/wood: late if submitted more than 4 days after arrivalDate; a future date is never late), stores it on the record, and the confirmation/CYA read-only view shows a banner naming the rule. Open: whether 'two days before' is calendar days or 48 hours; whether the potato time of arrival counts; whether to warn on CYA before submission (c-035); whether the engine exposes a derived-at-submit hook or the backend computes it. Conflicts c-002, c-029, c-031, c-035. | Ruling: Build it in the first pass as a stored system value: a pure lateness helper beside the check-answers feature computes on-time | late from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) using the c-031 calendar-day rule; the declaration POST calls it with the finalise clock and commits the result as the lateNotificationIndicator system value (manifest obligation, system: true, in SYSTEM_POPULATED) immediately before submitJourney when the journey is DRAFT, leaving it untouched on a re-submit from AMEND (c-030); the draft CYA calls the same helper with the request clock for its warning; confirmation, the submitted CYA and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value (c-035). No finalise hook, no backend field, no engine change. | Ruled at D1-territory-and-timing (d-007): RULED at D1: calendar-day rule per c-031 (potatoes late after arrivalDate minus 2, plants and wood late after arrivalDate plus 4; arrivalTime ignored; a future date is never late for plants and wood); computed by one pure helper beside the check-answers feature from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) and committed as the lateNotificationIndicator system value (manifest obligation, system: true, SYSTEM_POPULATED) in the declaration POST immediately before submitJourney when the journey is DRAFT, untouched on a re-submit from AMEND (c-030); the draft CYA warning calls the same helper with the request clock; no finalise hook, no mapper field (explicit omission assertion); shown per c-035 (draft CYA warning, confirmation and submitted-CYA banner reading the stored value, dashboard Late tag). PARKED: projecting the flag into the backend NotificationDto (no typed field — Mapper A). | Ruled at D6-chrome-and-journey-shape (d-073, day-one-critical-and-list-volatility): The two windows are the exported constants named in day-one-critical-and-list-volatility; the derivation and the commodity-type option hints read them, so a policy change to a window is a one-constant edit.

NNS-UN-001, NNS-UN-025 ('pre-nots' / 'post-nots') and NNS-UN-036 treat pre/post-movement status as something the importer must understand and that drives what is asked; the page never says whether the importer chooses it or the service derives it from the arrival date (annex:5/reg:26(2)(a)-(b) phrase it as either/or). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-006): a user-selected arrivalStatus radios page for plants and wood before the date and destination pages; potatoes have no status (c-002). Alternative: derive from arrivalDate being past or future (ambiguous on the day of arrival, and would reorder the arrival section). Gate question. | Ruling: Build the user-selected arrivalStatus radios page (Yes first) for plants and wood, placed before arrival-details and place-of-destination; potatoes have no status and skip the page by the derived gate. The service never derives the status from the date, in this run or later. | Ruled at D1-territory-and-timing (d-008): RULED at D1 (c-006): user-selected on the arrival-status page; derived gate, not authored (page.gate null per c-002); potatoes skip it; no date-based derivation; Yes radio first; the destination page's already-arrived copy covers the landed-but-in-transit case (reg 26(2)(b)).

The draft SI is England-only ('into England', 'arrival in England', 'landing in England' — annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)-(2)(a)) but reg 26(2)(b) says 'intended destination in Great Britain', the Policy section says 'arrival in GB', the user needs say 'imports into Great Britain' and the mural says 'EU -> GB'; Scottish Government is a competent authority (section:policy/para:7) and NNS-UN-029 wants Scottish regulators to see consignments in their region, yet nothing says how a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified. Actor: importer, policy. Proposed (c-001): 'Great Britain' in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading, arrivalDate labels, hint copy) and no territorial validation on the destination address. Open: whether the SI will be widened to GB, or the service must route Scottish destinations elsewhere. | Ruling: Build with 'Great Britain' in every notifier-facing string and no nation check on the destination address. The residual legal question — whether the draft SI is widened to GB or Scottish and Welsh instruments mirror it, and whether a Scottish or Welsh destination ever routes elsewhere — is recorded as PARKED (policy) inside this behaviour and changes no page. | Ruled at D1-territory-and-timing (d-009): RULED at D1 (c-001): Great Britain in all notifier-facing copy; no nation check on placeOfDestination; Scottish and Welsh destinations notify through this service. PARKED (policy): the draft SI is England-only (reg 24A(1), reg 26(1)-(2)(a)) and the paper contains no Scottish or Welsh instrument — whether the SI is widened or mirrored, and any per-nation routing, is revisited when the SI is laid; cross-referenced on competent-authority-routing.

The origin country list is constrained by what is being imported: ware potatoes only Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain (annex:5/reg:24A(1)(b)) with Spain excluding the Balearic Islands (reg 24A(3)); seed potatoes any part of the Common SPS Area other than the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man (reg 24A(1)(a)); plants for planting 'grown in, or from, a member State'; wood 'from a member State' except conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain only (reg 26(1)); the mural narrows ware potatoes to Spain and Poland (c-021). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-022): countryOfOrigin stays same-as-animals (autocomplete, always in scope, one obligation) over an EU-member-state block; the narrowing is validation inside POST from the set-owned commodities service, keyed on the categories present in commodityLines (the engine shape would be anyAllowListed); 'Spain (excluding the Balearic Islands)' is hint text. Open: whether an out-of-scope origin (ware potatoes from France) should be rejected, warned, or accepted as a notification the scheme does not require; whether the country block for plants is GBNAG_SPS_EX or a new one; whether a region option is needed for Spain. | Ruling: Build it in the first pass as page-side validation exactly as c-021 and c-022 rule: one countryOfOrigin autocomplete on the animals widget and service over GBNAG_SPS_EX (variant-of-animals — same widget and service); the origin POST rejects a country outside the intersection of the allow-lists for the categories present in commodityLines with the narrowing error naming the allowed countries; the Balearic inset (potato-scope-guidance) shows when a ware-potato line exists; Check your answers re-checks the same rule and refuses POST with a Change link to origin. The warn-or-accept alternative, a Spanish region option, a plants-specific block and the grown-in versus originate-from wording are parked. | Ruled at D3-origin-values-and-validation (d-056), superseding the 'Open:' sentence: RULED (panel, D3): validation inside the origin POST from sets/high-risk-plants/services/commodities over the GBNAG_SPS_EX list (c-022) — effective list = intersection of the per-category lists for the categories present in commodityLines (ware-potatoes PL/PT/RO/ES; conifer-wood-without-bark IT/FR/PT/ES; plants and other wood EU_MEMBER_STATES; seed-potatoes ANY_PRIMED_COUNTRY); an out-of-scope origin is rejected with the narrowingErrorCopy sentence naming the allowed countries; Balearic inset (potato-scope-guidance, c-021) when a ware-potatoes line exists; notification-view re-checks and refuses POST with a Change link to origin. PARKED: accept-or-warn instead of reject; a region option for Spain; a plants-specific block (country-block-decision); grown-in versus originate-from wording for potatoes (reg 24A(1)(b) vs 24A(2)(ab)).

category is always in scope on every line (no scope gate), so scope-and-wipe cannot purge lines whose category no longer belongs to a changed commodityType (skeleton scope-and-wipe, helper-selection-rule: a value-list mismatch is not a scope condition). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-013): the commodities list page reconciles on load — lines whose category is outside the new type's set are dropped with a notification banner — mirroring animals' reconcile-by-key on the search page (reconcileEntriesAt). Alternative: three typed collections (potatoLines, plantLines, woodLines) each gated on commodityType with wipeOnExit so the model does the wiping, at the cost of three collection pages and duplicated quantity fields. Alternative: retain lines and let validation flag them (NNS-UN-006 'flexible'). Gate question; a candidate model extension if Sam wants the model to own it. | Ruling: Build it in the first pass exactly as ruled in c-013: the commodity-type POST, after committing a changed commodityType, reconciles commodityLines with reconcileEntriesAt (keep lines whose category is in the new type's set, drop the rest with wipe semantics), the page warns before when lines exist, and it redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> where a notification banner reports the removal and the zero-lines redirect is suppressed for that load. The on-load reconcile, three typed collections and retain-and-flag alternatives are not built; a model-owned projection helper is recorded as a candidate extension. | Ruled at D2-commodity-model (d-029), superseding the text from 'Proposed (c-013):' onward: Ruled (c-013): the commodity-type POST, after committing a changed commodityType, calls state.reconcileEntriesAt(request, h, ["commodityLines"], keyOf, kept) with keyOf = category|genus|potatoVariety and kept = lines whose category is in category.input.valuesByCommodityType[newType]; the page renders govukWarningText when lines exist before the change; when any line was dropped the POST redirects to commodities?removed=<n> through kit.withChangeContext whatever exit control was pressed; the commodities list page renders a govukNotificationBanner from that count, suppresses its zero-lines redirect for that load and never writes on GET. Rejected for the first pass: reconcile on list-page load (writes on GET, or leaves stale lines counted complete by the hub, CYA and submit when the trader changes type from a CYA Change link); three typed collections (three groups, duplicated quantity/genus/commodityCode/use, three CYA cards); retain and flag (an unsubmittable notification the trader cannot fix from CYA). Parked model extension: a projection helper that filters a group's records by a notification-level scalar so the model can own the drop.

Animals bounds its arrival date to [today - 7 days, today + 6 months] (live-animals arrival.js:5, dateTextInRange, one clock read per request). No plants source gives a bound; the timing rules only define lateness and a late notification must be accepted (late-accepted-not-rejected; mural use case bullet:2). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-029): dateText only (a real calendar date), no window, lateness derived at submission. Open: a sanity window to catch typos (for example 1 year back to 1 year ahead), whether a potato date in the past should trigger an 'already arrived' question the SI does not have, and whether the picker should carry min/max attributes at all. | Ruling: Build arrivalDate as a real calendar date with no sanity window and no picker min/max, except a maximum of today when arrivalStatus = already-arrived, from one bounds helper beside arrival-details. A past expected date for potatoes does not trigger an arrived question — potatoes have no arrived state — it is accepted, the potato hint says what to enter, and it surfaces as late; the typo sanity window is parked. | Ruled at D1-territory-and-timing (d-010): RULED at D1 (c-029): dateText; no sanity window (parked — no source gives numbers); already-arrived capped at today (Europe/London) via dateTextInRange max only, data-max-date in that state and nothing otherwise; bounds helper beside arrival-details; no potato already-arrived question (not a reg 24A(2) matter — the c-002 hint line covers late potatoes).

The plants backend ReferenceNumberGenerator and the frontend stub adapter mint {YY}-{XXXXXX} with no type-code prefix, both flagged PENDING REQUIREMENTS; animals uses GBN-AG-; referenceNumber has a unique index so the prefix must be decided before real data exists (skeleton reference-number-format, backend-reference-prefix-absent; annex:6/generated-data/item:1). The plants type code is an open question on epic EUDPA-407. Actor: policy, backend. Proposed (c-023): a gated cross-repo fix extra (backend generator + REFERENCE_NUMBER_PATTERN + tests; frontend stub + any display copy) anchored before the confirmation page, blocked until the code is agreed; the journey strip, dashboard and confirmation show whatever the backend mints meanwhile. | Ruling: Parked: the plants type-code prefix is a policy answer nobody has (still an open question on epic EUDPA-407 as of this ruling). The first pass builds on the unprefixed {YY}-{XXXXXX} the backend and stub mint, shown verbatim in every display place; the gated cross-repo backend-reference-prefix extra stays on the backlog re-anchored to end (c-023) so its Sam gate does not halt the review section. | Ruled at D5-reference-status-and-lifecycle (d-063), superseding 'anchored before the confirmation page, blocked until the code is agreed': anchored at end (c-023), blocked until the code is agreed. RULED (panel, D5): parked pending the plants type code (EUDPA-407 open question, unanswered as of the ruling). The frontend never validates or parses the reference, so the journey builds on the unprefixed backend format shown verbatim; the cross-repo extra keeps its Sam gate at end and must land before the first persistent deployed environment because referenceNumber carries a unique index.

'Notification status' is generated data with no vocabulary (annex:6/generated-data/item:3); the engine and animals carry DRAFT / SUBMITTED / AMEND / DELETED; NNS-UN-020 wants compliance to be 'a reportable status rather than an inference'; policy expects checks, results and non-compliances to attach to the notification (annex:6/functional/item:8-9). Actor: regulator, importer. Proposed (c-024): notificationStatus = the engine lifecycle; lateness as a separate flag; check outcomes are inspector-side data that never change the importer-facing status in this run. Open: whether policy wants a richer status (Late, Selected for check, Checked, Non-compliant) visible to the importer, and what the dashboard tag should read. | Ruling: Adopt the engine lifecycle DRAFT / SUBMITTED / AMEND / DELETED with the animals tags Draft / Submitted / Amending / Deleted (blue / green / yellow / grey) on the journey strip, dashboard card and confirmation page as the notification status the importer sees; lateness is the separate Late tag and banner from lateNotificationIndicator. A richer importer-facing vocabulary is parked pending a policy vocabulary, and check outcomes never change the importer-facing status in this run. | Ruled at D5-reference-status-and-lifecycle (d-064): RULED (panel, D5, with c-024): notificationStatus = the engine lifecycle; the dashboard tag and journey strip read Draft / Submitted / Amending / Deleted and all four are reachable in the first pass (Amend is in scope, c-030); the Late tag on the dashboard card and the banners are the lateNotificationIndicator rendering, never a status value (annex:6/functional/item:2 asks for a highlight, not a status). A richer importer-facing status (late / selected for check / checked / non-compliant) is parked pending a policy vocabulary; check outcomes are inspector-side data and never change the importer-facing status.

Animals offers per-status dashboard actions (SUBMITTED: View, Amend, Copy as new, Delete; DRAFT: Resume, Copy as new, Delete; AMEND: Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete) with cancel-amend and delete confirmation pages, and the plants engine already reserves the amend/cancel-amend/copy/delete slugs and records-port operations (skeleton actionSlugsReserved). The policy paper covers only amend-before-submitting and 'says nothing about amending a notification after submission, cancelling one, what happens if the consignment does not arrive'; the user needs are silent except NNS-UN-041 (reuse = Copy as new, parked). Actor: importer, regulator. Proposed (c-030): no cancel-amend or delete PAGE in the spec; the dashboard shows Resume and View only until ruled; Amend, Copy as new and Delete are gate questions because a submitted notification is a statutory record the regulator may have acted on (spot-check scheduled). If ruled in, the two confirmation pages are copied from animals as chores anchored after the confirmation page. | Ruling: Adopt the animals post-submission action set minus Copy as new (per c-030): dashboard SUBMITTED View | Amend | Delete, DRAFT Resume | Delete, AMEND Resume | Cancel amendment | Delete; CYA read-only offers Delete when SUBMITTED and the Cancel amendment link when AMEND; the delete-notification and cancel-amend confirmation pages are chore extras copied from animals. Copy as new stays parked with reuse-previous-consignment. The policy questions — may a submitted plants notification the regulator has acted on still be amended or withdrawn, and does an amended arrival date re-run the timing test — are recorded as parked, not blockers; meanwhile the late flag freezes at the first submission. | Ruled at D5-reference-status-and-lifecycle (d-065), superseding the text from 'Proposed (c-030):' to the end: RULED (panel, D5, c-030): dashboard SUBMITTED: View | Amend | Delete; DRAFT: Resume | Delete; AMEND: Resume | Cancel amendment | Delete; CYA read-only offers Delete (SUBMITTED) and the Cancel amendment link (AMEND); the confirmation page restores the animals view-or-amend block. The delete-notification-page (before key:e2e-start-section) and cancel-amend-page (before key:e2e-review-section) chore extras copy the two confirmation pages from animals; the delete page soft-deletes DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AMEND. Copy as new and the Notification copied banner stay parked with reuse-previous-consignment (NNS-UN-041). The late flag is computed only when finalising from DRAFT and kept on a re-submit from AMEND (the backend re-stamps submittedAt). Parked policy questions, not blockers: whether a submitted notification the regulator has acted on may still be amended or deleted; whether an amended arrival date re-runs the reg 24A two-day / reg 26 four-day test; whether the backend should keep a first-submission timestamp.

'The digital solution will need to enable monitoring of the following: Number of notifications (by country and commodity); Number of checks (by country and commodity); % checks for each commodity; Number of non-compliances (pests/other); Summary of action taken following non-compliance; Time taken per notification; Time taken for spot checks; Attempted checks unable to be completed as commodity moved on' (section:reporting-requirements/para:3/item:1-8); 'Facilitate management information and report generation' (annex:6/functional/item:7). 'Enables live access for APHA inspectors to data in the system' (annex:6/functional/item:10) and NNS-UN-022 ('accurate and timely data') mean a submitted notification is visible to inspectors immediately — no batch hand-off. A finalise that throws re-renders the declaration with the recoverable-error message and never an optimistic confirmation; a not-ready submit returns to Check your answers. No queue, batch or optimistic confirmation may be introduced between the notifier's submit and the persisted record. Inspector-side live access to that record is backend and regulator-tooling work outside the notifier frontend, parked with outbox-and-gbnag-publishing-out-of-scope. | Ruled at D5-reference-status-and-lifecycle (d-066): RULED (panel, D5): a constraint, not a feature — the confirmation renders only after records.finalise has returned SUBMITTED (real adapter POST /notifications/{journeyId}/submit and stub alike); dateOfNotification is stamped by the persistence layer at finalise and is the operative time for the reg 24A / reg 26 timing tests; a finalise that throws re-renders the declaration with sharedCopy.recoverableError (500) and a not-ready submit redirects to notification-view — never an optimistic confirmation; no queue, batch or optimistic step may be introduced between submit and the persisted record. Inspector-side live exposure of the record is backend/regulator-tooling work parked with outbox-and-gbnag-publishing-out-of-scope and equal-access-defra-policy-sg-fc.

'Provides Defra Policy, Scottish Government and Forestry Commission with the same level of access to the data in the system as APHA' (annex:6/functional/item:11; section:summary/para:4 'APHA, Forestry Commission and Scottish Government will need access to the scheme'). Parity of internal access for Defra Policy, Scottish Government and the Forestry Commission is a multi-organisation user model for the regulator product, wholly outside the notifier frontend; the journey owes it only the full submitted record with no organisation-based withholding, which it already persists, and its one touchpoint — the confirmation naming all three competent authorities without preferring one — is already in the spec. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-083), prefixing the detail with 'PARKED, not rejected (Sam, standing ruling 2 — internal users and access models are out of this phase; recorded D7).': The notifier journey owes this only the full submitted record with no organisation-based withholding, which it already does; its one touchpoint is the confirmation page naming all three competent authorities without preferring one (the relevant plant health authority — APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government — may carry out a spot check). 'System is accessible (WCAG2.2AA)' (annex:6/non-functional/item:1). Actor: service owner. Covered per page by the fit-spec axe checks (wcag2a + wcag2aa on initial and error states, serious/critical fail) and the Lighthouse accessibility floor 0.70 (feature-test-conventions-and-axe, lighthouse-audit-per-page); axe tags cover WCAG 2.1, so the 2.2-specific criteria (focus appearance, target size, dragging, consistent help, redundant entry, accessible authentication) need a manual audit and an accessibility statement — neither exists in animals or the skeleton. Open: who owns the WCAG 2.2 audit and the statement the footer links to. | Ruling: Adopt at page level: every plants page ships the fit-spec axe check on its initial and validation-error states plus the Lighthouse accessibility floor, and the axe tag list is widened from the two WCAG 2.0 tags to ['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa','wcag22aa'] so the machine-checkable 2.1 and 2.2 rules actually run. The manual WCAG 2.2 audit and this service's own accessibility statement are parked, not built, and the footer's accessibility link is routed through the gated chrome extra. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-074), superseding 'axe tags cover WCAG 2.1, so the 2.2-specific criteria ... Open: who owns the WCAG 2.2 audit and the statement the footer links to.': RULED (panel, D7): adopted at page level through feature-test-conventions-and-axe and lighthouse-audit-per-page; no page increment may narrow the axe tag list or lower the 0.70 floor. Correction: axe-core's wcag2a/wcag2aa tags run WCAG 2.0 rules only — the 2.1 and 2.2 rules carry wcag21a/wcag21aa/wcag22aa, which feature-test-conventions-and-axe now includes. The 2.2-only criteria are largely served by design (govuk-frontend 6.x for focus appearance, target size and dragging; save-and-return, address-book-picker and cya-change-round-trip for redundant entry; the fixed footer and confirmation help block for consistent help) but a manual WCAG 2.2 audit is still owed. PARKED, not rejected: the manual audit (no source names an owner) and this service's accessibility statement — the footer link at shared/layout.njk:122 points at the generic https://www.gov.uk/help/accessibility-statement and is resolved under chrome-placeholders-and-service-name.

'Meets GDPR requirements' (annex:6/non-functional/item:3). Actor: service owner, data protection. Personal data in the notification: contactAddress (name of the person making the entry), contactNumber, contactEmail, consignor name and address, the Defra ID user. The paper specifies no lawful basis, privacy notice or retention period, and 'says nothing about record retention periods'. The layout footer's Privacy link is an animals placeholder. Open: privacy notice content and URL, retention of submitted notifications and drafts, and whether the address-book copy semantics (inline copy of the contact) create a second copy of personal data to govern. | Ruling: Park the governance items — lawful basis, privacy notice content and URL, retention of drafts and submitted notifications — because the policy paper supplies none of them and the panel must not invent them. What the first pass owes GDPR it already does: it collects only the Annex 5 matters plus the paper's Common Data (Article 9(7) OCR is the ceiling), scopes every record to the Defra ID organisation, takes no document upload, and keeps the footer Privacy link, whose destination resolves under the gated chrome extra. | Ruled at D4-parties-and-contact (d-013, c-025), superseding 'contactAddress (name of the person making the entry), contactNumber, contactEmail, consignor name and address': contactAddress (the nominated contact's name, address, telephone number and email address copied inline from the address book — c-025), consignor name and address. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-076), prefixing the detail with 'PARKED, not rejected (panel, D7).' and superseding the sentences from "The layout footer's Privacy link is an animals placeholder." to the end of the 'Open:' sentence: What the first pass owes GDPR it already does: it collects only the annex:5 matters plus the paper's Common Data (Article 9(7) OCR, to the extent strictly necessary, is the ceiling — no page may add personal data the paper does not list), scopes every record to the Defra ID organisation (dashboard-listing), takes no document upload, and keeps the footer Privacy link, whose destination (shared/layout.njk:114 -> https://www.gov.uk/help/privacy-notice, the generic GOV.UK notice) resolves under chrome-placeholders-and-service-name. Parked for policy and data protection before beta: (1) the lawful basis, stated in a service privacy notice; (2) that notice's URL; (3) a retention period for DRAFT and SUBMITTED records — the plants backend stamps expireAt = created + ttl days in non-production only and never in production (NotificationService.stampExpiry; NotificationAggregate.expireAt), so production retention is undefined; (4) the address-book inline copy on contactAddress is the same personal data held twice by the same controller — a retention question, not a new category.

'System is secure (userid & password to access for internal users)' (annex:6/non-functional/item:4); the paper says nothing about how external notifiers sign in. Actor: internal users, importer. The notifier frontend already enforces Defra ID OIDC sign-in (stub-mode-and-sign-in) and org-scoped data; internal userid/password access is another product.
