Whether policy accepts Defra ID as the external identity, and the mural's 'Register for new [GB product]' registration stage, are out of this phase. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-077), prefixing the detail with 'PARKED, not rejected (Sam, standing ruling 2 — users and sign-in models are out of this phase; recorded D7).' and superseding the 'Open: whether policy accepts Defra ID as the external identity ...' sentence: Defra ID OIDC sign-in in real mode, the stub session with auth still enforced in STUB_MODE, and organisation-scoped records stand as adopted under stub-mode-and-sign-in and dashboard-listing; nothing more is built. The SI puts no registration on the operator (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1) name only the professional operator who must notify). Parked: internal userid/password access (another product), whether policy accepts Defra ID as the external identity, and the mural's Register for new [GB product] stage (file:blueprint; a placeholder name).

'Available 24x7' (annex:6/non-functional/item:6) — timing windows are counted in days against arrival so a notifier must be able to submit at any hour; NNS-UN-009 (complete dependably whenever required); NNS-UN-026 (service owner: usable and reliable under varying demand); the mural sizes the service at 59k notifications a year, 26% of plant imports, with seasonal peaks implied (file:blueprint/left header card). Actor: service owner. Infrastructure, performance testing (k6) and the CDP platform SLA are outside the journey; the journey's contribution is save-and-return, recoverable-save banners and no long synchronous work at submit. Open: peak-load targets and the k6 suite for plants. | Ruling: Adopt the journey's share of 24x7 availability, which the engine already delivers: save-and-return, recoverable-save and stale-action banners that keep the user's answers, a synchronous submit with no long work, and a late-notification derivation computed in Europe/London so a submission at any hour is judged on the right calendar day. Nothing in the journey may gate submission by time of day. Peak-load targets and a plants k6 suite are parked as infrastructure follow-ons; platform availability is the CDP SLA. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-078), superseding 'Open: peak-load targets and the k6 suite for plants.': RULED (panel, D7): the journey's contribution is adopted through save-and-return, recoverable-save-and-stale-action, declaration-and-submit-gate and live-access-synchronous-submission (synchronous submitJourney -> records.finalise, no long work) and the Europe/London derivation on lateNotificationIndicator, so a notification made at any hour is judged on the right calendar day. The SI windows are counted in days with no hour-of-day cut-off (reg 24A(1) at least two days before; reg 26(1) no later than four days after), so nothing in the journey may gate submission by time of day. PARKED, not rejected: peak-load targets (no source gives one — the mural 59k a year is an annual volume) and a plants k6 suite (none exists in the plants frontend, the animals frontend or the tests repo); platform availability is the CDP SLA, outside this spec.

'Available in English & Welsh language' (annex:6/non-functional/item:7). Actor: importer, Welsh Language Standards. The copy seam (copyFor, copy.cy.js per feature, copy-parity) is adopted from animals (welsh-copy-seam) and every same-as-animals string carries the animals Welsh, but NO runtime locale toggle exists in animals or the plants engine (copyFor always resolves en), every cy file is machine-draft, and this spec invents no Welsh — variant and plants-only copy has no Welsh at all. Open: the locale switch (cookie / lang query / Defra ID preference), translator review before any Welsh ships, and whether English-only is acceptable for the first release. | Ruling: Park the live Welsh service: the first release ships English-only with html lang en, the copy seam stays exactly as adopted so every plants string lands in both locale files at once, no Welsh is invented, and the runtime locale switch is not built because it is new engine capability and no translation has been commissioned. The follow-on is written into the behaviour in full so it can be cut as one extra the day a Welsh Language Standards owner and translation exist. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-079), prefixing the detail with 'PARKED, not rejected (panel, D7).' and superseding the 'Open: the locale switch ...' sentence: The annex:6 requirement stands and the first release does not meet it: it ships English-only with html lang en so assistive technology reads the page correctly, and copyFor keeps resolving en (shared/copy.js:15-16 — locale selection plugs in via the locale argument when a second language is commissioned). Adopted now: welsh-copy-seam — every feature lands copy.en.js and copy.cy.js together under the copy-parity tripwire, MACHINE-DRAFT banners stay, animals Welsh is copied only where the English is verbatim animals, no Welsh is invented. Parked until a Welsh Language Standards owner and translation are commissioned, then cut as one extra: (1) a locale selector (a lang query that sets a cookie, read once per request and passed to every copyFor call and to kit.base so html lang follows it); (2) a language toggle in the service navigation and Welsh for the govuk-frontend component strings (back, error summary title, pagination, task list statuses); (3) translator review of every copy.cy.js, removing the MACHINE-DRAFT banners and supplying Welsh for every variant-of-animals and plants-only string; (4) IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST re-justified; (5) a fit spec per page asserting the Welsh render. The paper does not say whether English-only is acceptable for a first release; that is recorded against the release, not resolved.

'Standardise information as much as is possible' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8); NNS-UN-016/017 (coded, consistent values); NNS-UN-006 pulls the other way ('detailed and flexible product information'). Actor: regulator, importer. Coded in this spec: commodityType, category, genus, countryOfOrigin, proposedPlaceOfLanding, arrivalStatus, notificationStatus; free text because no source gives a list: species, commodityCode, quantity (unit), potatoVariety, potatoIntendedUse, eppoCode, sizeOfTree, phytosanitaryTreatments, use, the three identification numbers, consignmentNumber (c-011). Open: which of those policy wants as controlled lists (intended use options, treatment codes such as HT/KD, a variety register, EPPO code lookup) and who supplies them. | Ruling: Adopt as met to the extent any source allows: every element a source gives a list for is a coded value — commodityType, category, genus, countryOfOrigin (ISO alpha-2), proposedPlaceOfLanding (port code), arrivalStatus, notificationStatus — stored as codes, served from a set-owned or platform service and rendered through service label functions; every other element is free text with a max length. Controlled lists for intended use, treatment codes, a variety register, an EPPO lookup, a species catalogue and the commodity-code scheme are parked until policy names them; the optional 'use' is removed (c-014). | Ruled at D3-origin-values-and-validation (d-058; c-014 d-050), superseding 'use' in the free-text list (removed under c-014) and the 'Open:' sentence: RULED (panel, D3): coded where a source gives a list (commodityType, category, genus, countryOfOrigin, proposedPlaceOfLanding, arrivalStatus, notificationStatus — stored as codes, rendered via service labels), free text with a max length otherwise (c-011). Promoting a free-text element later is an input.widget change plus a values list on the set-owned commodities service, obligation id and stored string unchanged. PARKED pending policy: intended-use options, treatment codes (HT/KD), a variety register, an EPPO code lookup, a species catalogue and the commodity-code scheme.

'Include means of data validation' (annex:6/non-functional/item:9); NNS-UN-007 (confidence the information is complete and correct); NNS-UN-017 (trust accuracy). Actor: importer, regulator. Every element has a rule in this spec — membership for coded values, real-date for dates, whole number for quantity, max length for text — but NO format rule exists for any free-text element because no source gives one (c-011). Open: formats for commodity code (tariff scheme), EPPO code, the three identification numbers, contact number and email, arrival time; each is a new lib/validate factory with default messages in both copy files once ruled. | Ruling: Adopt as met by the rules the spec now carries: required-ness per the SI mandate; membership for every coded value including the per-category origin narrowing and its Check-your-answers re-check; a real calendar date for arrivalDate; a new HH:MM factory for arrivalTime; a whole number of 1 or more for quantity; the animals pattern for consignmentNumber; animals' max lengths for all other text; HTTP 400 with a GOV.UK error summary on every failure. contactNumber and contactEmail were removed under c-025 — the address-book API validates phone and email at source. Formats for commodity code, EPPO code and the three identification numbers are parked until a source names the scheme; each becomes one lib/validate factory with default messages in both copy files when ruled. | Ruled at D3-origin-values-and-validation (d-059), superseding the 'Open:' sentence: RULED (panel, D3, c-011): required-ness per the SI mandate; membership for coded values including the per-category origin narrowing with its notification-view re-check; dateText for arrivalDate; a new HH:MM time factory for arrivalTime; requiredIntegerInRange min 1 for quantity; the animals consignment-number pattern; animals max lengths elsewhere; contactNumber and contactEmail removed under c-025 (phone and email validated by the address-book API at source). PARKED (no source names a scheme): commodity-code format, EPPO format, supplier/producer/crop identification-number formats — each a later lib/validate factory with default messages in both copy files once ruled.

'Minimise effort and potential disruption to traders' (annex:6/non-functional/item:10); 'The efficiency of the scheme, to show it is not overly onerous to trade' (section:reporting-requirements/para:2/item:2); NNS-UN-004 ('simple ... minimal effort', bold on the page); Article 9(7) OCR caps data at what is strictly necessary. Actor: importer, policy. Met in this run by: only the statutory matters plus Common Data are asked; scope hides irrelevant questions; save-and-return; address-book picks instead of typed addresses. Open and parked: reuse-previous-consignment, bulk-upload, import-from-existing-documents — the three effort-savers the needs ask for. The 'time taken per notification' MI metric measures this. | Ruling: Adopt: the first pass meets the requirement by asking only the Annex 5 matters plus the paper's Common Data, hiding questions outside the commodity's scope, save-and-return, address-book picks and change-from-CYA. Article 9(7) OCR makes this a ceiling as well as a goal — every question must trace to the SI or the Common Data list and no increment may add one that does not; any future optional question carries '(optional)' and never gates readiness. The three effort-savers stay parked under their own behaviours, bulk upload by Sam's ruling. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-080), superseding 'Open and parked: reuse-previous-consignment, bulk-upload, import-from-existing-documents — the three effort-savers the needs ask for.': RULED (panel, D7): met by proportionate-questions-by-scope, scope-and-wipe-on-exit, single-question-heading-convention, save-and-return, address-book-picker, cya-change-round-trip and amend-before-submitting. Article 9(7) OCR is a ceiling as well as a goal: every question must trace to annex:5/reg:24A(2), reg:26(2) or the paper's Common Data list (annex:6 — Name of person making entry, Contact number, Contact address, Contact email), and no increment may add one that does not. consignmentNumber is the one optional obligation and already carries (optional) and never gates readiness (c-003); any later optional question follows the same rule — its label carries (optional) per the GOV.UK Design System and it never gates submit readiness. The three effort-savers stay parked under their own behaviours: bulk-upload (Sam, standing ruling 3), reuse-previous-consignment and import-from-existing-documents (out per the brief).

'Sustainable' (annex:6/non-functional/item:5) — unqualified; no journey-level consequence stated by any source. Actor: service owner. Recorded so the Annex 6 list is complete; nothing in the spec depends on it. Open: what policy means (environmental, financial, maintainable). | Ruling: Park. 'Sustainable' is a single unqualified word in the only source that uses it, nothing in the journey depends on it, and the panel adopts no reading; the behaviour stays so the Annex 6 list is complete, and policy is asked what was meant before anything hangs on it. | Ruled at D7-non-functional (d-081), prefixing the detail with 'PARKED, not rejected (panel, D7).' and superseding 'Open: what policy means (environmental, financial, maintainable).': Parked for policy to define (environmental, financial or maintainability); the panel adopts no reading. If maintainability is meant, the M0 hygiene extras (dependabot-frontend, dependabot-backend, docs-drift-sweep, the copy tripwires) already serve it; no increment follows from any reading until policy says which.

Wood scope conditions: conifer wood with bark or isolated bark from any member State; conifer wood without bark only from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain; cut coniferous trees only when greater than 3 metres in height; wood of Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only when it retains its natural round surface or is in unprocessed chips; preservative-treated wood excluded from every item except cut trees (annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i)-(iv); h4:Additional caveats for wood products/li:1-4; file:data-fields/region:Wood/bullet:1-4). Actor: wood importer (NNS-UN-013). Proposed (c-007): the category values encode the item and its form; preservative treatment, the 3-metre threshold and the bark condition are hint and guidance copy, not questions — a wood importer whose consignment is outside scope simply does not notify. Open: whether policy wants explicit pre-scope questions ('Is the wood preservative-treated?') so out-of-scope consignments are caught, and whether an out-of-scope answer should end the journey with a 'you do not need to notify' page. | Ruling: Build the guidance reading: the five wood category values encode the SI items with the bark, origin, height and form conditions in their labels, and the preservative exclusion is a hint on the category question for wood notifications with its cut-coniferous-trees exception (the c-007 edit); no pre-scope question and no 'you do not need to notify' page. Fuller scope text belongs with guidance-before-you-start, outside the journey pages. Explicit scope questions that end the journey are parked pending a policy answer, not built. | Ruled at D2-commodity-model (d-030), superseding the text from 'Open: whether policy wants explicit pre-scope questions' onward: Ruled: guidance only — the five category value labels carry the bark, origin, height and form conditions and category.input.hintByCommodityType carries the preservative exclusion with its cut-coniferous-trees exception (c-007); fuller scope text belongs with guidance-before-you-start, outside the journey pages. Parked (needs policy): explicit pre-scope questions ("Is the wood preservative-treated?") and a "you do not need to notify" exit page — no source asks for either and Article 9(7) confines the data to the matters; revisit if the policy paper is reissued with screening rules.

Seed potatoes are in scope 'grown or suspected of having been grown in another part of the Common SPS Area, other than in the United Kingdom, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man' (annex:5/reg:24A(1)(a); mural use case 'Seed potatoes from any EU country'); ware potatoes only from Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain (reg 24A(1)(b)) where 'Spain' excludes the Balearic Islands (reg 24A(3)); the mural says Spain and Poland with an off-board footnote (c-021). Actor: potato importer (NNS-UN-011). Proposed: the seed/ware split is the per-line category, the origin narrowing is validation (origin-value-list-by-commodity), and 'excluding the Balearic Islands' is hint text on the origin page when a ware-potato line exists. Open: 'suspected of having been grown' — whether the notifier must declare suspicion; a region-level origin option for Spain; the mural footnote. | Ruling: Build it: the seed/ware split is the per-line category; the origin narrowing is validation owned by origin-value-list-by-commodity (its reject-or-accept question stays open there); the ware-potato origin scope and the Balearic Islands exclusion are one govukInsetText on the origin page, rendered page-side only when a ware-potatoes line exists, so countryOfOrigin's label, hint and widget stay verbatim animals (the obligation is tagged variant-of-animals for its validation and error sentence — c-022, c-027). 'Suspected of having been grown' is not asked; a Spain region option and the mural's off-board footnote are parked. | Ruled at D2-commodity-model (d-031), superseding the text from "Open: 'suspected of having been grown'" onward: Ruled: the seed/ware split is the per-line category; the origin narrowing is validation owned by origin-value-list-by-commodity (its reject-or-accept question stays open there); the ware-potato origin scope and the Balearic exclusion are a govukInsetText on the origin page when a ware-potatoes line exists, page-side so countryOfOrigin's hint stays verbatim animals. Parked (needs policy or reference data): a declaration of "suspected of having been grown" (not a reg 24A(2) matter, so not asked); a region-level origin option for Spain (no region list in any plants source); the mural asterisk footnote. | Ruled at D3-origin-values-and-validation (d-054, c-021): RULED D3 (c-021): four-country list PL, PT, RO, ES enforced in the origin POST; Spain stored as ES; Balearic exclusion is the origin-page inset per potato-scope-guidance. PARKED: a region-level option for Spain (no ISO 3166-2 in the countries service); whether the notifier must declare suspected origin (grown or suspected of having been grown, reg 24A(1)(b), versus the collected matter the country from which the potatoes originate, reg 24A(2)(ab)); the mural footnote.

'The information captured by PHNSS will be the same as was required under the previous notification system but with some additional requirements (see annex 2)' (section:policy/para:5; section:general-questions/para:1/item:1) and 'Similar notification systems are used in Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland' (section:summary/para:6; section:legal-basis/para:1). Actor: design research, policy. No extractor could read the previous scheme's form or the NI/RoI services; they are precedents for page copy, the 'intended use' options and the identification-number formats this spec lacks. Open: obtain the pre-2021 national notification scheme's data list and the NI/RoI screens as a design input before the copy pass. | Ruling: Parked as a copy and value-list input only, with no first-pass change. The SI data list (annex 5, reg 24A(2) and reg 26(2)) already fixes what is collected — the previous scheme cannot add or remove a matter — so the pre-2021 scheme and the NI/RoI services can only refine page copy, the potato intended-use options and the identification-number and commodity-code formats, all of which the spec leaves as free text with validationRaw 'none given'. A precedent-driven change lands later as a copy-pair or lib/validate edit, never a model change. Needed: the pre-2021 national notification scheme's data list and the NI/RoI notification screens, obtained by policy or design research before the copy pass. | Ruled at D6-chrome-and-journey-shape (d-072): Ruled D6 (panel), PARKED: no first-pass change. Annex 2 equals the SI matters, so the previous scheme cannot change WHAT is collected. Affected slots are potatoIntendedUse (options), supplierIdentificationNumber / producerIdentificationNumber / cropIdentificationNumber / commodityCode (formats) and every page or obligation carrying provisionalCopy — each is free text with validationRaw none given, so a precedent lands as a copy-pair or lib/validate change, never a model change. Needed: the pre-2021 scheme data list (the policy team's own general question 1) and the NI/RoI notification screens, from policy or design research before the copy pass.

'The PHNNS has been identified as a day 1 critical need' for when the SPS agreement enters into force (section:summary/para:5; section:legal-basis/para:4) — no date given; the document is Version 1 August 2026 with draft SI text, so the statutory wording, the commodity list and the timing windows are all subject to change (docProps:core; annex:1/closing-para); the mural blueprint is 'Alpha Phase Confirmed - Update as Required'. Actor: delivery, policy. Consequence for the build: every list is data behind the set-owned service; every window is one constant in the lateness derivation; the England/GB strings are copy leaves — so a policy change is a data or copy change, not a model change. Open: the go-live date and who re-runs the digest when the paper is reissued. | Ruling: Adopted as a standing build constraint on every increment: (1) every commodity-type, category, genus and origin list is data behind the set-owned commodities service, never an obligation or copy literal; (2) the two statutory timing windows are single named constants — POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL = 2 (reg 24A(1)) and PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL = 4 (reg 26(1)) — exported from one module beside the arrival-details feature and read by the lateness derivation and by any hint that names a window, so no other copy of the number exists; (3) the England / Great Britain wording and the authority names are copy leaves. A reissued policy paper is then a data or copy change, never a model change. The go-live date and who re-runs the digest are delivery notes outside the spec. | Ruled at D6-chrome-and-journey-shape (d-073), superseding 'Open: the go-live date and who re-runs the digest when the paper is reissued.': Ruled D6 (panel), ADOPTED as a build constraint: (1) commodityType, category, genus and origin lists live in the set-owned commodities service, never in obligation or copy literals (annex:1/closing-para; annex:6/functional/item:4); (2) the timing windows POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL = 2 (reg 24A(1)) and PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL = 4 (reg 26(1)) are exported from one module beside the arrival-details feature and are the only place a window is written — the lateness derivation and any hint naming a window read them (copy functions take the day count as an argument; hint copy quotes it, never recomputes it); (3) England / Great Britain wording (c-001) and the authority names are copy leaves only.
